svg.text: 1. Suffering is not the objection; senselessness is.
"Not suffering, but the senselessness of suffering was the curse" that lay over humanity
man "wills it, he even seeks it out, provided that he is shown a meaning for it"
2. The ideal gave suffering a meaning, the only one so far, at a price.
"any meaning is better than no meaning"; "the door to all suicidal nihilism was closed"
"it brought all suffering under the perspective of guilt": new, deeper suffering
the faute de mieux; life as a bridge (§11), suffering as punishment (§20)
3. The will was saved: a will to nothingness is still a will.
"a will opposed to life, a repudiation of the conditions of life, but it is and remains a will!"
lieber will noch der Mensch das Nichts wollen, als nicht wollen
man would still rather will nothingness than not will: §1's sentence, earned about the sick
what it commits the author to: a counter-ideal that gives suffering a meaning without guilt
Ecce Homo on GM: "a counter-ideal was lacking, until Zarathustra"; Module 6's problem
